title: THC Simple User Guide
subtitle: A starter path from setup to cure.
intro: What stage you are in → what the plant needs → what to do → what to avoid → what comes next.
lawfulUseNotice: Use this guide only where home cultivation is lawful. Follow local law, product labels, safety instructions, and building/electrical rules.
visualStatus: Batch 1 learner copy has been fact-corrected and locked for layout. Final visuals still need text QA before approval.

pages.title: Setup
pages.lead: Get ready before you start seeds.
pages.simpleRule: Set up first. Start seeds second.
pages.goal: Show that the grow space must be ready before starting seeds.
focus: Plan drying and curing before harvest

learnMore.label: Go deeper: environment and grow-space basics

pages.title: Seeds
pages.lead: A seed wakes up with moisture and warmth.
pages.avoid: Drowning it or checking too much.
focus: Seeds need moisture, warmth, and patience
Do not drown or overhandle the seed
Move on when the root appears

pages.title: Seedling
pages.lead: A seedling is a baby plant.
pages.avoid: Too much water, food, or strong light.
focus: Use gentle light and light watering

pages.title: Veg
pages.lead: Veg is when the plant grows bigger.

sections.label: Do
sections.text: Water when the pot starts to dry.

pages.goal: Teach that veg is the plant-building stage.
focus: Veg builds roots, stems, leaves, and branches

pages.title: Flower
pages.lead: Flower is when buds begin to form.

sections.label: Needs
items: For photoperiod plants: 12 hr light / 12 hr uninterrupted dark
Lower humidity as buds get dense
Bloom-stage feeding: less nitrogen than veg, with adequate phosphorus and potassium

pages.avoid: Wet, stale air around buds; light leaks for photoperiod plants; overfeeding.
pages.moveOn: Buds getting bigger and smell getting stronger.
pages.goal: Teach that flower is the bud-forming stage and patience matters.

pages.title: Harvest
pages.lead: Harvest means cutting the plant when buds are ready.
pages.avoid: Harvesting wet plants or cutting before the drying space is ready.
pages.simpleRule: Harvest when the plant is ready.
pages.goal: Teach not to harvest too early.

pages.title: Dry
pages.lead: Drying slowly removes moisture after harvest.
pages.avoid: Heat, bright light, and direct fan blast.
pages.moveOn: Buds feel dry outside; small stems bend with a light snap. Do not make buds bone-dry.
pages.simpleRule: Fast drying can ruin good flower.
pages.goal: Teach drying as a critical step, not an afterthought.
focus: Use gentle airflow, not direct fan blast

pages.title: Cure
pages.lead: Curing is the final step after drying.

sections.label: Do
sections.text: Open containers early if moisture builds up. If jar humidity stays high, dry longer.

pages.goal: Teach cure as the final finishing and storage step.

pages.title: Pests & Disease
pages.lead: Pests and diseases can damage plants.

sections.label: Do
sections.text: Look under leaves often and keep the space clean.

pages.avoid: Random sprays, harsh chemicals, or spraying buds.
pages.simpleRule: Catch problems early and fix safely.
pages.goal: Teach early problem spotting without turning the page into pest science.
focus: Look for bugs, spots, webs, eggs, and damage
Do not spray random products on buds

pages.title: Tips

sections.label: Beginner rules that matter most
items: Change one thing at a time

pages.goal: Give a new grower practical survival rules.
focus: Change one thing at a time

learnMore.label: Go deeper: observation and grow records

revisionNotes: Corrected flower stage to say 12/12 applies to photoperiod plants, not autoflowers.
Changed pest page to Pests & Disease so mildew and disease signs are not mislabeled as pests.
Replaced casual neem/random-spray guidance with label-safe, crop-safe wording.
Changed dry endpoint from hard stem snap to a safer beginner description: dry outside with a light snap, not bone-dry.
Added lawful-use and safety notice outside the learner card copy.
